title: Detect Flapping Machines
description: Read-only deterministic analysis that detects flapping TPU machines and mass events in one zone's GCE system-event timeline, grouping outages by physical host via mapping_file (when provided) or by GCE instance ID; keying by instance ID alone can undercount when node-pool and MIG recreates split one machine's history across VM names and instance IDs. Heuristics: outage = hostError or terminateOnHostMaintenance (assumption, not from the source), merged within 15 min; mass event = >= 5 machines with outages within 15 min (reported separately, no per-host strikes); flag at >= 3 outages in 24 h, >= 2 strikes in 14 d (outages >= 2 h apart outside mass events) or >= 3 maintenance windows opened in 24 h, the *_24h counts being the max over any rolling 24 h (assumption, not from the source). Inputs: [[query-gce-system-events-by-zone]] and an optional instance-to-host mapping JSONL. Thresholds are heuristics from past TPU7x repairs, not SLOs.

events_file.description: Path to the JSON array written by [[query-gce-system-events-by-zone]] (its default output_file is scratch/gce_system_events.json). Query with a start up to 14 d back so the strike window is covered.

mapping_file.description: Optional JSONL produced by an instance-to-host mapping export, possibly several daily runs concatenated (from the day before the oldest sighting, at most ~15 days back). When provided, groups outages by physical host; when empty, falls back to keying by GCE instance ID, which undercounts across VM recreates.

limit_used.description: The limit passed to [[query-gce-system-events-by-zone]] when events_file was written (its default is 50000); used to detect truncation.
